stories.title: China urges respect for digital sovereignty in AI race
stories.summary: BEIJING, Aug 19 - China on Wednesday urged respect for each country's digital sovereignty, after a report the U.S. would ask countries to choose sides in the artificial intelligence race with Beijing.
article_sentences: China on Wednesday urged respect for each country's digital sovereignty, after a report the U.S. would ask countries to choose sides in the artificial intelligence race with Beijing.
China is opposed to taking sides and forming camps on AI, its foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said at a regular briefing.

stories.title: Vietnam seeks to clear land before compensation in overhaul plan
stories.summary: The issue is becoming more pressing as Vietnam embarks on vast urban and infrastructure projects.
article_sentences: Vietnam has proposed allowing land clearance to begin before compensation and resettlement plans are finalised, a major change that could speed up development projects but raise concerns about safeguards for residents.

The proposal is intended to “remove institutional bottlenecks and unlock land resources to serve socio-economic development and the goal of double-digit growth in the new period”, according to a statement on the government website.
Under the plan, the authorities would not have to wait for payment and relocation arrangements to be completed, potentially shortening lengthy clearance processes.
Affected residents would receive priority for compensation in the form of land or housing at the site.
The issue is becoming more pressing as Vietnam embarks on vast urban and infrastructure projects.
A US$28 billion (S$35 billion) overhaul of Hanoi’s Red River corridor alone is expected to require about 200,000 people to move from their homes.
The city’s chairman has said replacement housing, services and livelihood opportunities should be ready before trying to move people.
The South-east Asian nation is targeting economic growth of at least 10 per cent in 2025 and investing heavily in infrastructure as it seeks to achieve high-income status by 2045.
Land-clearance disputes, however, have held up some major developments and have long fuelled social tensions in Vietnam.
Farmers often complain that official payouts fall below market prices, while the process can be vulnerable to corruption.
Some grievances have erupted into protests, including a 2020 clash over land rights in Dong Tam commune that killed four people.
One high-profile case involves a Trump Organization-branded golf resort in northern Hung Yen province.

stories.title: Plantwatch: Cities make a surprising refuge for threatened UK wildflowers
stories.summary: Nooks and crannies in urban areas provide a welcome alternative to intensive farming and other rural pressures Wildflowers are having a rough time in the countryside, mostly from the onslaught of intensive farming with fertilisers, pesticides and herbicides and less grazing. On top of that, there are building developments, competition from invasive plant species and the climate crisis to contend with. The UK has lost 97% of its wildflower meadows over the last century and over half of the country’s native flowers have been in decline for 70 years. Continue reading...
